rationale: A randomized Parkinson trial of daily 100 mg whole saffron powder tablets reported depression scores 4.58 points lower than placebo (95% CI 0.81 to 8.34 lower) on the registered secondary measure. The separate Tehran capsule trial favored saffron on Hamilton scores, with inconclusive secondary mood measures and unverified capsule preparation. Outside Parkinson disease, the two linked Shiraz reports used shared fluoxetine and give conflicting counts and inconclusive between-arm results. Older extract and combination studies used different preparations. The Parkinson trials still give a lean against the frozen worsening hypothesis, with transfer to ordinary culinary use uncertain.

In a four-person Parkinson espresso crossover average secondary fatigue ratings were lower with caffeinated espresso in three people and higher in one with no pooled effect. Both conditions used brewed coffee, and the run-in and washout allow caffeine withdrawal. The Nurses’ Health Study separately reports fatigue by broad diet pattern; the supplement combines coffee and tea and gives no individual coffee contrast. The isolated caffeine comparisons and other populations leave brewed-coffee effects on Parkinson fatigue unresolved.

Injected isolated safranal shortened hindlimb release time in a mouse stiffness assay. The randomized Tehran saffron capsule trial reported an inconclusive total motor comparison and no separate rigidity result; capsule preparation remains unspecified. The combination extract and crocin studies likewise give aggregate motor outcomes. Clinical rigidity after ground saffron consumption remains unresolved.
